prompt.context_jp: 課長として説明を求める里中の声は、いつになく尖っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 課長として説明を求める里中の声＿、いつになく尖っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks 里中の声 as the topic being described.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is describing a known entity (Satonaka's voice) and commenting on it — classic topic-は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the voice as new, identifying information, but here it's the topic the narrator is characterizing.

contrast_examples.en: A sharp voice (new info) could be heard.

prompt.context_jp: 福岡さんをかばう場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 福岡さん＿悪くないです 部長に言われて やっただけです
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that defends Fukuoka contrastively.

feedback.correct_en: は carries contrastive nuance: 'Fukuoka (as opposed to whoever's really at fault) is not to blame.' The speaker is deflecting responsibility away from her.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it a neutral identification ('Fukuoka is not bad'), losing the defensive contrast against the real culprit (the department head).

contrast_examples.jp: 私は知らない(けど他の人は知ってる)。

prompt.context_jp: 「部長に言われて やっただけです」と聞いた後。
prompt.prompt_en: Satonaka reacts to newly revealed information. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: Satonaka is identifying the surprising new agent: 'The department head (did this)?' が marks the newly-identified subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 部長 an already-established topic, losing the shock of discovering who ordered the shredding.

contrast_examples.en: As for the boss? — asking about him as topic.

prompt.context_jp: エレベーターホールで親子連れが立ち尽くしている場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 近づいてきたの＿、通りかかったばかりの大前春子だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Identify who it was that approached.

feedback.correct_en: The 'Xのは Yだ' cleft structure uses は to set up the described event as topic and names Y as the identifying answer.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would break the cleft structure; 近づいてきたのが大前だった sounds like exhaustive listing out of context and is less natural here.

contrast_examples.en: The one who came is him.

prompt.context_jp: 大前が商品を評価する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 黒豆ビスコッティ＿ 黒豆と穀物の香りがする おいしいお菓子です
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the product as the topic being described.

feedback.correct_en: Omae is commenting on a known product (the biscotti) — classic topic-は followed by a description.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would identify which snack is delicious among options; here she simply characterizes the already-known product.

contrast_examples.jp: このお菓子はおいしい。
このお菓子がおいしい。
contrast_examples.en: THIS snack is the delicious one (among choices).

prompt.context_jp: 宇野部長に厳しく言われた後。
prompt.prompt_jp: 宇野の言葉＿、東海林の胸を鋭く抉った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle framing Uno's words as the topic.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator sets 'Uno's words' as the topic, then describes their effect. This reflective narrative tone takes は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it sound like identifying which thing pierced his heart, as if contrasting with other candidates.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の言葉は心に残った。
contrast_examples.en: His words stayed in my heart (topic).

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の言葉が心に残った。
contrast_examples.en: It was his words that stayed (identifying).

prompt.context_jp: シュレッダー室で。
prompt.prompt_jp: シュレッダー＿ クロスカットでなかったのは 不幸中の幸いです
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the subject of the embedded clause (のは cleft)?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a 〜のは〜 nominalized clause, the subject takes が because は is reserved for the main topic (the outer のは).
feedback.incorrect_en: Using は inside the subordinate clause would clash with the outer topic は of the cleft structure.

contrast_examples.en: It was yesterday that he came (が in subord. clause).

prompt.context_jp: 復元作業中の緊張した場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 里中の指先＿ 微かに震えている。
prompt.prompt_en: Narrative description of Satonaka's fingertips.

feedback.correct_en: Observational description of a physical state uses が — the narrator notices the fingers trembling as a fresh observation.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'his fingertips' a topic being contrasted or characterized, which doesn't fit the live-observation feel.

prompt.context_jp: 謝罪会見前の東海林の弁明。
prompt.prompt_jp: 無理だ ごまかすしかない それ＿会社の方針だ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle identifies 'that' as (exhaustively) being the company policy?

feedback.correct_en: それが会社の方針だ identifies/pinpoints 'that' as what the company policy is — exhaustive identification.
feedback.incorrect_en: それは会社の方針だ would merely comment on 'that'; the emphatic identifying nuance ('that is precisely the policy') needs が.

prompt.context_jp: 謝罪を求められている場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 東海林の頭＿ 下がらなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Narrative statement about his head.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator establishes 東海林の頭 as the topic and reports a negative fact ('his head, it did not bow'). Negative statements about topics strongly prefer は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly identify which thing did not bow, as if from a set. The topical reading is natural here.

contrast_examples.en: HE was the one who didn't apologize.

prompt.context_jp: 東海林が商品を擁護する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 黒豆ビスコッティ＿本物です！
prompt.prompt_en: East-sea-forest insists the PRODUCT (vs. the data) is genuine.

feedback.correct_en: Contrastive は: 'The product (as opposed to the falsified data) IS real.' The whole speech pivots on separating product from falsification.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively pinpoint ('the biscotti is the real thing [among options]'), which doesn't capture the contrast against the fraudulent data.

contrast_examples.jp: データはウソですが、商品は本物です。
contrast_examples.en: The data is a lie, but the product is genuine (contrast).
The product is the real one (identifying).

prompt.context_jp: 謝罪会見での訴え。
prompt.prompt_jp: でも あの商品に ウソ＿ありません！
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits 'there is no lie in that product'?

feedback.correct_en: Contrastive は with negation: 'lies — those, there are none (in the product).' This カテゴリー-focus pattern (Xはない) is standard for emphatic denial.
feedback.incorrect_en: ウソがありません is grammatical but sounds like a plain existence statement; は brings the contrastive 'as for lies, there are none' nuance that matches his defiant tone.

prompt.context_jp: 電話が鳴りやまない理由を伝える。
prompt.prompt_jp: 違いますよ 黒豆ビスコッティの注文＿ 殺到してるんですよ
prompt.prompt_en: Delivering surprising new info about orders.

feedback.correct_en: Fresh, surprising event introduced into the conversation ('orders are pouring in!') — new-information が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'orders' a topic already under discussion, losing the revelatory punch.

contrast_examples.en: As for orders, they're not flooding in (topic/contrast).

prompt.context_jp: 社長の意図を宇野が説明。
prompt.prompt_jp: 君＿ 13年間 本社から離れていた
prompt.prompt_en: Addressing Tokairin about his history.

feedback.correct_en: Directly addressing 東海林 as the topic ('As for you, you were away for 13 years') — topic-は.
feedback.incorrect_en: 君が would identify who was away (as if answering 'who was away?'), but here Uno is characterizing Tokairin's background.

prompt.context_jp: 大前が自分の立場を説明する。
prompt.prompt_jp: いえ ＿ですが 何か？
prompt.prompt_en: Omae identifies her employment status.

feedback.correct_en: 派遣 (haken, dispatch/temp worker) is Omae's defining identity in this drama and the correct term she uses.
feedback.incorrect_en: 社員 would mean regular employee (what she isn't); バイト is 'part-timer', a different category.

prompt.context_jp: 友造が北海道からわざわざ来た理由。
prompt.prompt_jp: ＿いられないさ
prompt.prompt_en: 'I couldn't just sit still.' Choose the set expression.

feedback.correct_en: 居ても立ってもいられない is a fixed idiom meaning 'can't stand still from worry/anxiety' — exactly what Tomozo feels.
feedback.incorrect_en: 寝ても覚めても means 'waking or sleeping' (constantly); the other option is invented and not idiomatic.

contrast_examples.jp: 心配で居ても立ってもいられない。
contrast_examples.en: I'm so worried I can't sit still.

contrast_examples.jp: 寝ても覚めても彼女のことを考える。
contrast_examples.en: I think of her day and night.

prompt.context_jp: 宇野が謝罪会見のアドバイス。
prompt.prompt_jp: いざとなったら ＿して終わらせろ
prompt.prompt_en: Extreme form of apology in Japanese business culture.

feedback.correct_en: 土下座 (dogeza) — kneeling with head to the floor — is the ultimate apology gesture, exactly what Uno orders as a last resort.
feedback.incorrect_en: 正座 is just sitting formally on knees; 会釈 is a slight bow — neither carries the apologetic/submissive weight needed here.

prompt.context_jp: シュレッダー済みの紙を復元すると宣言する大前。
prompt.prompt_jp: ジグソーパズル＿1級の 大前春子です
prompt.prompt_en: Omae has countless certifications. What word fits?

feedback.correct_en: 検定 is used for certification/proficiency exams (like 漢字検定, 英語検定). ジグソーパズル検定1級ホルダー fits Omae's running joke about her many qualifications.
feedback.incorrect_en: 試験 is a generic 'test/exam'; 大会 is a 'competition/tournament' — neither captures the 'Level 1 certified' framing.

prompt.context_jp: 記者が宇野の言い訳を追及。
prompt.prompt_jp: このような状況で つい ＿ということ自体 あり得ないですよね
prompt.prompt_en: Mimicking Uno's excuse — 'carelessly/by accident'.

feedback.correct_en: うっかり = 'carelessly/absent-mindedly,' which is exactly the excuse Uno offered (つい うっかり) and that the reporter is throwing back at him.
feedback.incorrect_en: しっかり means 'firmly/properly' — the opposite; ばっちり means 'perfectly' — also wrong direction.

prompt.context_jp: 東海林が謝罪会見で悪化させる様子。
prompt.prompt_jp: 火に＿ 注いじゃってますよ
prompt.prompt_en: Idiom: making a bad situation worse.

feedback.correct_en: 火に油を注ぐ ('pour oil on fire') is the Japanese idiom for making things worse — exactly what the apology is doing.
feedback.incorrect_en: Pouring water on fire would extinguish it (opposite meaning); 風 doesn't form an idiom here.

contrast_examples.en: Put water on the fire (literal, not idiom).

prompt.context_jp: 大前が切り札を差し出す場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: こんなことも ＿かと
prompt.prompt_en: Trademark phrase meaning 'I anticipated this might happen.'

feedback.correct_en: こんなこともあろうかと is a set literary expression using the volitional/presumptive あろう ('in case something like this might happen') — the classic 'I prepared for this' line.
feedback.incorrect_en: あるだろうか sounds like a question; あって is a te-form that doesn't complete the set phrase.

contrast_examples.jp: こんなこともあろうかと用意しました。
contrast_examples.en: I prepared, anticipating this might happen.

contrast_examples.jp: こんなことがあるだろうか。

prompt.context_jp: 大前が宇野部長に釘を刺す。
prompt.prompt_jp: 派遣の力を＿と えらい目に遭いますよ
prompt.prompt_en: 'If you ___ the power of temps, you'll regret it.'

feedback.correct_en: 侮る (あなどる) = 'underestimate / look down on' — exactly Omae's warning about dismissing temp workers.
feedback.incorrect_en: 崇める is 'to worship' (opposite); 任せる is 'to entrust' — doesn't match the warning tone.

contrast_examples.en: If you underestimate your opponent, you'll lose.

prompt.context_jp: 大前が里中に素っ気なく答える場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line fits Omae's characteristic blunt, deadpan style?

choices.text: 忘れ物を取りに来ただけですが 何か？
忘れ物を取りに来ただけなんですよ〜

feedback.correct_en: 〜が 何か？ is Omae's signature deadpan closing — flatly polite but confrontational, perfectly in character.
feedback.incorrect_en: The 〜なんですよ〜 variant sounds soft and chatty, totally at odds with Omae's cool professional detachment.

contrast_examples.en: I'm a temp. Got a problem?
Well, I'm a temp, you see~ (soft).

prompt.context_jp: 謝罪会見の冒頭、社長の挨拶。
prompt.prompt_en: Which opening is natural for a formal press apology?

choices.text: 本日は お忙しい中 お集まりいただきまして 誠にありがとうございます
今日は 忙しいのに 来てくれて 本当にありがとう

feedback.correct_en: お集まりいただきまして・誠にありがとうございます is the standard 謙譲語+formal register required at corporate press conferences.
feedback.incorrect_en: The casual variant would be jaw-droppingly inappropriate at a public apology — it reads like thanking friends.

contrast_examples.jp: ご来場いただき誠にありがとうございます。
来てくれてありがとう。

prompt.context_jp: 大前が浅野に帰れと言う場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds like Omae?

choices.text: そんなことより とっとと嫁の元へ帰りなさい
そんなことより 早く奥さんのところへ帰ったほうがいいですよ

feedback.correct_en: とっとと + 命令形 帰りなさい captures Omae's curt, bossy-older-coworker register that drives the comedy.
feedback.incorrect_en: The softer 〜ほうがいいですよ advice form sounds considerate and polite — not Omae's biting style.

contrast_examples.en: Hurry up and go home! (curt command)

contrast_examples.jp: 早く帰ったほうがいいですよ。
contrast_examples.en: You should go home soon (gentle advice).

prompt.context_jp: 大前が東海林を叱咤する。
prompt.prompt_en: Which emphasizes 'apologize in YOUR OWN words' naturally?

choices.text: 自分の言葉で謝りなさい
自分で言葉を謝りなさい

feedback.correct_en: 自分の言葉で (with で marking means) idiomatically means 'in your own words' — the natural collocation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 自分で言葉を謝る is ungrammatical — you can't 'apologize words'; 言葉 needs で to mean 'by means of (one's own) words'.

prompt.context_jp: 大前が原稿を手渡す場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrase sounds natural in a dramatic business comeback scene?

choices.text: 読んでください 大逆転スピーチです
読んでください とても逆転なスピーチです

feedback.correct_en: 大逆転 is a natural compound noun ('major turnaround') that modifies スピーチ directly — the standard way to intensify 逆転.
feedback.incorrect_en: 逆転 isn't a na-adjective, so とても逆転な is ungrammatical. Intensification uses the 大〜 prefix instead.

contrast_examples.jp: とても成功なプレゼン。
